sections.html:
Concord is the capital of New Hampshire and the seat of Merrimack County, about 16 miles north of Manchester and 66 miles north of Boston. Property tax here is a city, county and school matter, so first learn which part of the city your house is in. The villages are Penacook, Concord Heights, East Concord and West Concord, and downtown has its own North End and South End neighborhoods.

Penacook is served by the Merrimack Valley School District rather than the Concord School District, so the district depends on where the house sits. Homes near the Merrimack River and its tributaries should be checked against the FEMA flood map. Winters test roofs, heating systems and insulation every year.

Concord bills twice a year and collects in four installments. The July and October bills are estimates, each 25 percent of the prior year's total bill. The January and March payments are final and are adjusted for the earlier estimates.

InstallmentDue dateType
FirstJuly 1Estimate
SecondOctober 1Estimate
ThirdJanuary 2Final, adjusted
FourthMarch 31Final, adjusted

The July and October bills are mailed together around June 1, and the January and March bills go out around December 1. Bills are based on the April 1 assessment under RSA 76:2. State law requires 8 percent interest on late balances, prorated daily, and the city cannot waive it.

The Tax Collector is at 41 Green Street, 603-225-8540. Hours are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, and Thursday 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM. You can pay online, by phone, in person, or by mail to the City of Concord Tax Office, PO Box 9582, Manchester, NH 03108. Send mailed payments 7 to 10 days before the due date.

The 2025 rate is $29.11 per $1,000 of assessed value. It breaks down as $10.18 for the city, $2.54 for the county, $1.58 for the state education tax and $14.81 for the local school district. The rate was set on November 19, 2025, on a valuation of $4,967,453,081 and a total commitment of $154,257,720.

Your own assessment decides your bill. The local school rate is the largest piece, and if your house is in Penacook or another part of the city, confirm your exact rate with the city assessor at 603-225-8550.

Concord completed a citywide revaluation to bring assessments to full and true market value as of April 1, 2026. The New Hampshire Constitution requires values to be set anew at least once every five years, and the previous revaluation was in 2021. New assessments are finalized before the final 2026 tax bill in December 2026, and abatement applications are available in the Assessing office after December 1, 2026.

  • Compare your new assessment with recent sales of similar houses.
  • File an abatement application if you think the value is wrong.
  • If you are selling, expect a buyer to underwrite the new value rather than your old one.

Apply to the city for an abatement by March 1 following the notice of tax. Under RSA 76:16, a person aggrieved by an assessment who has complied with RSA 74 may apply in writing by March 1, and the city must grant or deny in writing by July 1. A failure to respond counts as denial. For the current cycle the deadline is March 1, 2027.

If the city denies your request, the denial letter must explain the next appeal step. You can go to the Board of Tax and Land Appeals, phone 603-271-2578, or to superior court. The state sets the abatement form, so get the current one from the city or the Board.

Unpaid tax can become a tax lien and, eventually, a tax deed, but the process takes at least two years. Under RSA 80:76, the collector executes a deed to the lienholder after 2 years from the execution of the lien if the land is not redeemed. At least 30 days before the deed, the collector must notify the owner under RSA 80:77 and mortgage holders under RSA 80:77-a, by certified mail.

The title company pays unpaid tax from your proceeds, so a sale while the lien is still redeemable resolves it. Interest runs at 8 percent on late balances, so waiting makes the payoff larger.

New Hampshire's real estate transfer tax is $0.75 per $100 of the price, and it is imposed on both buyer and seller. It is filed and paid online through Granite Tax Connect. For questions, call the Department of Revenue Administration at 603-230-5920. Your purchase and sale agreement says who bears the cost in practice, so read the closing costs line carefully.

A cash sale is the shortest path to closing, and a listing may fit a house in good condition. A cash buyer takes the house as-is, so a Concord property with deferred roof work, tenants or a tax balance can still sell.

  • Get a payoff statement from your lender and a balance from the Tax Collector.
  • Find your 2026 assessment and compare it with your old one.
  • Request a written offer and check who pays each closing cost.

We buy Concord houses as-is and do not charge commission or fees to the seller.

faqs.q: When are Concord property taxes due?
faqs.a: Installments are due July 1, October 1, January 2 and March 31. July and October are estimates of 25 percent of the prior year's bill, and January and March are the final adjusted payments.

faqs.q: What is the Concord tax rate?
faqs.a: The 2025 rate is $29.11 per $1,000: $10.18 city, $2.54 county, $1.58 state education and $14.81 local school.

faqs.q: What is the interest on late Concord property tax?
faqs.a: State law requires 8 percent interest, prorated daily, on balances past the due dates, and the city cannot waive it.

faqs.q: What is the abatement deadline in Concord?
faqs.a: Under RSA 76:16, applications are due by March 1 after the notice of tax. The deadline for the current cycle is March 1, 2027, and forms are available in Assessing after December 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Who pays the New Hampshire transfer tax?
faqs.a: Both buyer and seller. The rate is $0.75 per $100 of the price, filed and paid online through Granite Tax Connect.
